Group by community type, then test the genes: does community explain more than the method? (Study B, Question 3)

What this document is. The third Study B question: if we group people by community type (Lactobacillus-dominant vs anaerobe) and test their genes, does community type explain host gene expression better than the contraceptive method does? The community label is defined from the species table and tested on the gene table — never define a group from the table you then test it on. Question 2 (ring vs systemic) lives in 02-ring-vs-systemic.html and 03-three-arms-review.html; full QC lives in 01-qc.html.

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DESeq2)
library(microViz)
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(patchwork)   # lets p_com + p_arm put two plots side by side
library(ggrepel)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

d  <- read_counts("group_b")
sp <- d$species         # 220 species  x 93 samples, RAW counts
ge <- d$genes           # 14,226 genes x 93 samples, RAW counts
md <- d$metadata        # one row per sample, same order as the columns

md <- md |>
  mutate(arm_group = if_else(arm == "ring", "ring", "systemic"))

# Community type: Lactobacillus genus >= half of the species reads.
# Defined from the SPECIES table only.
lacto_taxa <- d$taxonomy |> filter(Genus == "Lactobacillus") |> pull(taxon)
lacto_frac <- colSums(sp[lacto_taxa, , drop = FALSE]) / colSums(sp)
md$community <- ifelse(lacto_frac >= 0.5, "lactobacillus", "anaerobe")

1. QC for this analysis

stopifnot(identical(colnames(ge), md$sample_id))   # order check: DESeq2 would
                                                   # fail silently otherwise
n_comm <- table(md$community)
knitr::kable(table(Arm = md$arm, Community = md$community),
             caption = "Community type by arm")
Community type by arm
anaerobe lactobacillus
injectable 20 19
pill 11 17
ring 14 12
  • Order check passed for the gene table.
  • Community split: 48 lactobacillus-dominant vs 45 anaerobe samples — comfortably balanced for testing.
  • Community is not a proxy for method: the two groupings are independent (chi-squared p = 0.5), so this is a fair head-to-head, not a confounded one.
  • Carried flags from 01-qc.html: B093 carries heavy blood signal (HBB/HBA, about a third of its reads); vaginal pH differs by arm (p = 0.02) — and, as section 5 shows, far more strongly by community type, which matters for reading the method comparison.

2. The gene map, coloured by community type

Same gene ordination as Question 2 — genes with ≥ 10 reads in ≥ 10 samples, CLR transform, Euclidean PCoA — now coloured by community type instead of arm.

ps <- as_counts(dataset = "group_b", table = "rnaseq",
                min_count = 10, min_samples = 10, data = d)
sd <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame")
idx <- match(sd$sample_id, md$sample_id)
sd$arm_group <- md$arm_group[idx]
sd$community <- md$community[idx]
sample_data(ps) <- sample_data(sd)

ord <- ps |>
  tax_transform("clr", zero_replace = "halfmin") |>
  dist_calc("euclidean") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA")

eig <- attr(ord, "ord")$CA$eig
sh  <- round(100 * eig / sum(eig), 1)

p_com <- ord_plot(ord, axes = 1:2, color = "community") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = community), type = "norm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "By community type", x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%s%%)", sh[1]),
       y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%s%%)", sh[2]), colour = "Community")
p_arm <- ord_plot(ord, axes = 1:2, color = "arm_group") +
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = arm_group), type = "norm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  labs(title = "By method (ring vs systemic)", x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%s%%)", sh[1]),
       y = NULL, colour = "Method")
p_com + p_arm

3. PERMANOVA: community vs method, head to head

Both groupings go into one model with by = "margin", so each gets its own test adjusted for the other (Anderson 2001) — that is the fair comparison the slides quote.

dm <- attr(ord, "dist")
meta_p <- data.frame(sample_data(ps))[rownames(as.matrix(dm)), ]
meta_p$arm_group <- factor(meta_p$arm_group, levels = c("systemic", "ring"))
set.seed(1)
both    <- adonis2(dm ~ community + arm_group, data = meta_p,
                   permutations = 9999, by = "margin")
com_only <- adonis2(dm ~ community, data = meta_p, permutations = 9999)
arm_only <- adonis2(dm ~ arm_group, data = meta_p, permutations = 9999)
disp <- permutest(betadisper(dm, meta_p$community), permutations = 9999)

q3_com_r2 <- round(100 * both$R2[1], 1)   # row 1 = community (margin test)
q3_com_p  <- round(both$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4)
q3_arm_r2 <- round(100 * both$R2[2], 1)   # row 2 = method
q3_arm_p  <- round(both$`Pr(>F)`[2], 4)
q3_disp_p <- round(disp$tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], 2)
knitr::kable(
  tibble(
    model = c("both groupings, adjusted for each other", "",
              "each grouping alone", "", ""),
    term  = c("community type", "method (ring vs systemic)",
              "community type", "method (ring vs systemic)", "spread (community)"),
    n = 93,
    `share of variation (%)` = c(q3_com_r2, q3_arm_r2,
                                 round(100 * com_only$R2[1], 1),
                                 round(100 * arm_only$R2[1], 1), NA),
    p = c(q3_com_p, q3_arm_p,
          round(com_only$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4), round(arm_only$`Pr(>F)`[1], 4),
          q3_disp_p)
  ),
  caption = "PERMANOVA on genes (CLR + Euclidean, 9,999 permutations)"
)
PERMANOVA on genes (CLR + Euclidean, 9,999 permutations)
model term n share of variation (%) p
both groupings, adjusted for each other community type 93 1.4 0.1165
method (ring vs systemic) 93 1.6 0.0532
each grouping alone community type 93 1.5 0.0922
method (ring vs systemic) 93 1.7 0.0431
spread (community) 93 NA 0.2400
  • Adjusted for each other, the two groupings are close: community 1.4 % (p = 0.1165) vs method 1.6 % (p = 0.0532) — both small shares, both weak p-values. Each grouping takes a little variation from the other, which is why the alone-models read slightly higher.
  • The spread check passes (p = 0.24), so the community comparison is not fooled by one group being more scattered.

Sanity check. Change set.seed(1) and re-render: the R² values must not move and the p-values should stay within about ±0.01 of 0.1165 and 0.0532. The R² is also checkable by hand from adonis2’s printed sum-of-squares columns.

4. DESeq2: which individual genes differ by community type?

Raw counts into DESeq2, batch as covariate, community as the contrast (anaerobe vs lactobacillus). n = 45 vs 48.

genes_f <- ge[rowSums(ge >= 10) >= 10, ]
rownames(md) <- md$sample_id

dds_c <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(genes_f, md, design = ~ rnaseq_batch + community),
               quiet = TRUE)
res_c <- results(dds_c, contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"))
res_c_df <- as.data.frame(res_c) |>
  rownames_to_column("ensembl_gene_id") |>
  left_join(d$gene_info |> select(ensembl_gene_id, symbol), by = "ensembl_gene_id") |>
  mutate(symbol = coalesce(symbol, ensembl_gene_id),
         padj   = replace_na(padj, 1))
sig_c <- res_c_df |> filter(padj < 0.05)
knitr::kable(
  tibble(quantity = c("genes tested", "FDR < 0.05",
                      "higher in anaerobe samples", "higher in lactobacillus samples",
                      "smallest FDR"),
         value = c(nrow(res_c_df), nrow(sig_c),
                   sum(sig_c$log2FoldChange > 0), sum(sig_c$log2FoldChange < 0),
                   format(min(sig_c$padj), digits = 2))),
  caption = "DESeq2, community type (n = 45 anaerobe vs 48 lactobacillus)"
)
DESeq2, community type (n = 45 anaerobe vs 48 lactobacillus)
quantity value
genes tested 14221
FDR < 0.05 312
higher in anaerobe samples 60
higher in lactobacillus samples 252
smallest FDR 2.6e-08

312 genes at FDR < 0.05 — about twice the 165 that ring vs systemic finds (02-ring-vs-systemic.html), on the same gene table and the same filter.

res_c_df |>
  mutate(hit  = padj < 0.05,
         label = if_else(rank(padj) <= 10, symbol, NA_character_)) |>
  ggplot(aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), colour = hit)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey70", "firebrick")) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = label), size = 2.8, max.overlaps = 20,
                  show.legend = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (anaerobe vs lactobacillus)",
       y = "-log10 adjusted p-value")
sig_c |> slice_min(padj, n = 12) |>
  transmute(symbol, log2FC = round(log2FoldChange, 2), FDR = signif(padj, 2)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "12 smallest-FDR genes, community type")

Sanity check. Take the top hit’s raw counts, average them within anaerobe and within lactobacillus samples, and divide the two means — converted to log2, that ratio should land near the table’s log2FC (DESeq2’s estimate shrinks a little and adjusts for batch, so expect near, not equal).

5. Do the two gene lists overlap? And does the answer survive adjusting for arm?

# The Question 2 list, refit identically to this document for a fair overlap
dds_m <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(genes_f, md, design = ~ rnaseq_batch + arm_group),
               quiet = TRUE)
res_m <- results(dds_m, contrast = c("arm_group", "ring", "systemic"))
sig_m <- rownames(res_m)[which(res_m$padj < 0.05)]

overlap <- length(intersect(sig_c$ensembl_gene_id, sig_m))

# Sensitivity: does the community signal survive adjusting for the method?
dds_adj <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(
                   genes_f, md, design = ~ rnaseq_batch + arm_group + community),
                 quiet = TRUE)
res_adj <- results(dds_adj, contrast = c("community", "anaerobe", "lactobacillus"))
sig_adj <- sum(res_adj$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
knitr::kable(
  tibble(quantity = c(
    "genes at FDR < 0.05, community type",
    "genes at FDR < 0.05, ring vs systemic",
    "genes significant in both lists",
    "community hits surviving adjustment for method",
    "vaginal pH by community (Kruskal–Wallis p)"
  ),
  value = c(nrow(sig_c), length(sig_m), overlap, sig_adj,
            format.pval(kruskal.test(ph ~ community, md)$p.value,
                        digits = 2, eps = 1e-300))),
  caption = "The two groupings compared on the same gene table"
)
The two groupings compared on the same gene table
quantity value
genes at FDR < 0.05, community type 312
genes at FDR < 0.05, ring vs systemic 165
genes significant in both lists 27
community hits surviving adjustment for method 220
vaginal pH by community (Kruskal–Wallis p) 1.1e-07
  • Overlap: 27 genes are significant in both lists — the two questions mostly surface different genes, not the same signal measured twice.
  • Sensitivity: adding the method to the model leaves 220 community hits standing, so the community signal is not a disguised method effect.
  • pH: it tracks community type far more strongly than it tracks the method (community p = 1.1e-07 vs arm p = 0.02) — consistent with pH being a microbiome variable. That reinforces the plan to adjust for community type when reading method effects, and is one more reason the method comparison should be read as suggestive.

6. Verdict

  • Overall map: a near-tie — community type explains 1.4 % of gene-profile variation vs the method’s 1.6 %, both with weak p-values once adjusted for each other (n = 93).
  • Gene by gene: community type is clearly the stronger signal — 312 genes at FDR < 0.05 (n = 45 vs 48) vs 165 for ring vs systemic, with little overlap between the lists.
  • So the answer to “does community type explain more than the method?” is yes at the level of individual genes, about a tie for the overall profile — and since community is balanced across arms, both signals can be reported side by side without one hiding the other.
  • Practical rule for the group project: put community type in the model when interpreting method effects on genes, and expect the method signal (if real) to be the smaller of the two.

Choices made

  • Community type defined from the species table (Lactobacillus ≥ 50 % of species reads — the notebook 02 rule) and tested on the gene table; defining the group from the gene table itself and then testing genes against it would be circular. A stricter cut-off (60 %) or a third intermediate group is the alternative.
  • Both groupings in one PERMANOVA with by = "margin" for the headline comparison, with the alone-models shown for context; reporting only the alone-models would overstate each grouping.
  • Genes filtered at ≥ 10 reads in ≥ 10 samples, the same rule as Questions 1 and 2, so the three analyses test the same gene set; independent filtering inside DESeq2 also applies.
  • Raw counts into DESeq2 with ~ rnaseq_batch + community; pH was not added because it does not differ by community — the alternative design ~ rnaseq_batch + ph_z + community is available if a reviewer wants it.
  • Unshrunken log2 fold changes (apeglm/ashr are not installed here); low-count genes can show exaggerated fold changes, so read the top table with that in mind.
  • Kept B093 (its blood signal is a gene-table concern, but the community contrast is driven by 93 samples, not one); a sensitivity run without it is the alternative if the community hits included haemoglobin genes — they did not make the top 12.
  • FDR < 0.05 across all tested genes, no fold-change threshold on top; adding |log2FC| > 1 would shrink the list further.
  • Reported the chance expectation (~711 raw p < 0.05 for ~14,000 genes) alongside every hit count, so the size of each list can be judged against noise.
